thread:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a perf dip on qa cluster after the FAv3 rollout to the hetero pool. Throughput down ~12% for mixed seqlen workload.
ben: ugh. can you paste the perf numbers? batch size, GPU, model? :thinking_face:
maria: short summary:
- model: redwood-open-7b
- hw: A100-40GB
- batch: inflight continuous batching (auto)
- workload: 30% seqlen 16, 50% seqlen 64, 20% seqlen 512
- metric: tokens/s down ~12% vs FAv2 fallback baseline
oliver: did we fall back to a different kernel shape? FAv3 has a different workspace strategy — might be fragmenting the workspace pool for short sequences.
sana: any logs from kernel decision telemetry? maybe kernel selector picked fa_v3 small-block kernels for midseq that are slower on this mix.
maria: attached profiler snippet (reduced):
```
kernel_choice: fa_v3_block(64,32) x 45%
kernel_choice: fa_v3_block(128,32) x 30%
kernel_choice: fa_v2_block(64) x 25%
avg_token_latency: 8.6ms -> 9.7ms
```
ben: interesting that fa_v2 still used. Might be thresholding logic that prefers fa_v3 when seq<=256 but fa_v3 has more launch overhead per micro-batch.
oliver: also check KV cache allocation churn — fa_v3's workspace allocator uses per-request scratch by default, leading to extra cudaMemset/cudaFree noise on hetero loads.
sana: can we repro quickly with a synthetic mix? i can run a micro-bench harness hitting exactly the seq distribution.
maria: please do. also try setting kernel_selector.debug=1 and workspace.mode=shared in config to see if it stabilizes.
runtime-bot: scheduled job run/1715004321-repro-1 started by sana (queue: perf-harness)
ben: hypothesis: continuous batching accumulates many short contexts into a larger effective qk length, causing fa_v3's blocking to increase memory thrash. alternative: fa_v3 tuned for long contiguous sequences — when we interleave many short requests it loses efficiency.
oliver: actionable experiments:
1) run synthetic mix against fa_v2 and fa_v3 with same batching policy (no autoscale)
2) force workspace.mode=shared vs per-request to measure memcpy/free churn
3) instrument kernel-launch counts and average block dims
4) try small micro-batch coalescing (aggregate up to N requests) to see if latency improves
sana: running (1) now. will push results to thread. adding a variant where we pin to single-stream execution to remove concurrency noise.
maria: if repro holds, we might change selector heuristic: prefer fa_v2 when >X% of requests are below seq Y AND concurrency>Z. but want to avoid a big rule list.
ben: could we learn the selector threshold automatically? maybe a tiny cost model that estimates per-request execution time for each kernel using trace histograms. then pick kernel with lowest expected cost across the current batch.
oliver: that's the long-term solution — online cost-model. short-term patch: adjust fa_v3 activation threshold up (require longer sequences) and prefer shared workspace for hetero pools.
sana: repro results (quick):
```
fa_v2 tokens/s: 12.3k
fa_v3 (default) tokens/s: 10.8k
fa_v3 + workspace.shared: 12.0k
fa_v3 + single-stream: 11.2k
```
maria: wow workspace.shared brought it almost back. suggests allocator churn is a big factor.
ben: ok prioritize a fix: default workspace mode for hetero routing -> shared. also add selector telemetry flags so we can capture distribution at decision time.
oliver: i'll open a tiny RFC for selector-telemetry + new default for hetero pools. include a safe rollout (canary + metric gates on p95 latency and tokens/s).
maria: also want an e2e test in perf harness that simulates mixed seqlen to avoid regressions.
sana: filed repro job artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/fa3-mixedseq/1715004321
runtime-bot: ticket RUNTIME-5247 created by oliver: "fa_v3 workspace default and selector telemetry for hetero pools" (priority: high)
ben: thanks. follow-ups: add micro traces for cudaMemset/cudaFree counts, kernel launch time histogram; and we should evaluate quantized kernels too.
maria: agreed. will add to the RFC checklist. thanks team :thumbsup:
